chunks: Ali, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Yunus, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The slave, when he steals from his masters, is not cut (hand); so if he steals from other than his masters, he is cut.

key_terms.يُقْطَعْ: He is cut (referring to the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for a slave who steals?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the application of the hadd punishment for theft by distinguishing between intra-household theft from one's master, which is exempt, and theft from outsiders, which incurs the standard penalty. This ruling reflects the juristic view that the master's ownership extends to the slave's possessions, making theft from the master akin to taking from one's own property, whereas theft from others constitutes a distinct violation of rights.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Salih Bin Saeed, from Yunus, from one of our companions, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The owned (slave), when he steals from his master, he would not be cut. So if he steals from other than his master, he would be cut’.
